title: The Indus Waters Treaty has no exit clause for one side
sources: Indus Waters Treaty, Karachi, 19 September 1960 (UN Treaty Series vol. 419, No. 6032): Articles I(5)-(6), II(1), III(1), XII(3)-(4)
India: MEA special briefing, 23 April 2025; Government of India statement, 31 August 2026 (Tribune; Al Jazeera)
Pakistan: National Security Committee statement, 24 April 2025 (Radio Pakistan; Dawn)
Court of Arbitration (Indus Waters Western Rivers Arbitration), award of 31 August 2026 (Tribune; Al Jazeera)

quiz.q: Which rivers go to India under the treaty?
quiz.why: Right. Article II gives India unrestricted use of the Eastern Rivers: the Sutlej, Beas and Ravi.

scenes.sub: Modified or ended only by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose

claims.claim: The treaty was signed at Karachi on 19 September 1960 (1960)
Eastern Rivers (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi) are available for the unrestricted use of India (Art. I(5), II(1)); Pakistan receives the Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) (Art. I(6), III(1))
Article XII (3)-(4): the treaty may be modified, and continues in force until terminated, only by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the two Governments
claims.quote: shall continue in force until terminated by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose

claims.claim: On 23 April 2025 India announced the treaty would be held in abeyance with immediate effect until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism
claims.quote: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 will be held in abeyance with immediate effect

claims.claim: On 24 April 2025 Pakistan's National Security Committee said the treaty contains no provision for unilateral suspension
On 31 August 2026 the Court of Arbitration unanimously held that India's abeyance decision was impermissible and the treaty remains in force
India rejected the 31 August 2026 award, called the court illegally constituted, said it has never recognised it, and said abeyance remains in force

review_note: SERIOUS and strictly neutral: treaty text plus each side's formal statements with dates, no verdict and no characterisation. Treaty text from the UN Treaty Series (primary); India's April 2025 statement from the MEA briefing transcript on an Indian embassy site (primary). Pakistan's statement and the August 2026 award and India's response come from two news sources each; the award text itself was not read. Left out on purpose: Pakistan's 'act of war' wording, the Pahalgam attack details, the Ratle/Kishenganga merits, the Neutral Expert process, the June 2025 supplemental award, any figures on water flows. Exit-clause title is accurate to Article XII(4): no unilateral termination clause. Re-check status immediately before release; this topic moves.
